analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md was supplied, as full head text (units :8 and :9, lines 1-231 and 232 onward). It is documentation only, so the file adds no executable behavior or trust-boundary change. The newest entry (line 3) says GET /v1/cache/status will now count `artifact_allowlist.stale_models` and add Prometheus and Datadog gauges. It also says the coordinator log will name each live artifact tuple once. The entry states that routing and the exact-match allowlist rule are unchanged. That relates to T-041/SEC-035 (cache routing and cross-tenant prefix-cache scope). The code behind it was not supplied, so these points need review in the real code diff:
1. Whether /v1/cache/status is authenticated or admin-gated, and whether the new counts expose model artifact tuples or weight hashes.
2. Whether logging live tuples leaks sensitive identifiers.
3. Whether the allowlist is still matched exactly (no fuzzy or revision-agnostic fallback), which would weaken per-account cache scoping.
Other changelog entries look like pre-existing documentation of earlier releases. They include the T-031 earnings-endpoint removal, the fail-closed attestation challenges, the App Attest protocol 3-only rule, and the SEC-035 TTL re-acceptance at 30 minutes. I cannot tell from this unit alone which lines are new in the diff. I found no concrete security regression in the changelog text itself.
